evidence.blockers: Ten P1 items requiring manual verification across five areas: the new YYYY.WW.N version scheme on all downstream consumers, the /v1/docs HTTP endpoint and lemonade_docs MCP tool, the candidate publishing pipeline end-to-end, the FLM download path with ModelScope integration, and the HF architecture filter affecting model downloads and API latency. No P0 blockers detected.
evidence.breaking_changes: The version scheme shifted from M.m.p to YYYY.WW.N[~count.hash] with CMakeLists.txt no longer using a static VERSION declaration — it invokes python3 tools/version.py at configure time. The MSI installer now uses @LEMONADE_MSI_VERSION@ (YY.MM.PATCH) instead of @PROJECT_VERSION@, the Windows assembly manifest uses @LEMONADE_NUMERIC_VERSION@, and the get-version action output format changed to YYYY.WW.N.
evidence.coverage: 38 commits reviewed across the range; 2 commits in this range have no commit review and are not covered in this digest.
evidence.manual_testing: Testers should verify: (1) the /v1/docs index endpoint returns a correct JSON index with the running version and individual pages fetch valid markdown, (2) the lemonade_docs MCP tool responds correctly with a standard MCP client, (3) the FLM download path with default_model_source=modelscope correctly passes --modelscope 1 to the flm binary in both load-time and explicit pull paths, (4) the candidate publishing pipeline creates unsigned MSI builds with candidate-v* tags and proper release notes on a release-v* branch, and (5) downstream consumers (MSI, Fedora, Debian, Snap, Docker) handle the new YYYY.WW.N version format correctly, particularly the YYYY field exceeding 255 in MSI version fields.
evidence.security: No security concerns observed in the reviewed commits. The wildcard origin feature (6a5e307) maintained strict scheme enforcement. The revert of the internal MCP client (496bb24) removed an attack surface. The GGUF architecture filter (6a60710) improves security by rejecting incompatible repositories before download. No credential handling, supply-chain changes, or suspicious code patterns detected.

verdict_reason: Five manual verifications before shipping: the new version scheme on downstream packages, the /v1/docs API and MCP tool, the candidate publishing pipeline, the FLM download path with ModelScope, and the GGUF architecture filter — none are P0 blockers, but none can be skipped.
